budgets.basis: zero-logic pin-register seam pair, DFFHQNx1 (die_ci_margins.json lib), 60/25 ps uncertainty (AGENTS.md), xtalk_default; data wire delay ignored

placement: (a) receiving tile, input path (chosen): hierarchical sign-off practice is top-down timing budgeting -- the top level hands each block IO constraints (set_input_delay -min/-max) derived from the top clock plan, the block closes them in its own flow (Cadence/Synopsys budgeting, ETM/ILM blocks), and the top only verifies.  Here the seams are ABUTTED (no die-top rows between neighbours), the receiver already owns its face flops and its FF hold repair (run_kit.sh FF GRT step), one value per type port covers every instance, and the delay sits on the receiver's own input net, so no new die-top placement, no ECO on a routed die and no hand edit.  (b) die-top cells in channels/bays: only where a channel exists; it would need std-cell rows + PG + a die-level repair step on the abutted seams, breaks tile self-containment and puts the cells far from the receiving flop -- kept as the fallback for channel crossings only (gen_phys keeps the fallback contract on channel ports).
